interactions.title: The ash in the Mirror of the Past
lines: DM: So while you're helping the rangers get the perimeter established around Isingue as the ash has stopped falling, one evening you take a moment to pull the Mirror of the Past out of your portable hole, and take the pile of ash that Kenzo or Seeker, I forget who, grabbed from the decaying elemental as you killed her in the plane of Limbo, and hold it up to the mirror.
DM: And as you do, you see an image. For, for a minute, it's hard to track. It's, uh... Too many things are changing at once.

DM: But as you watch, it seems to be recognizably a land of some sort. Like, there's... It's not, it's clearly not Limbo. It's like a, a place where there is a sky and a ground, but the ground is constantly shifting.
DM: And you can see the same person, the, the Queen of Ash, um, running along a, like up a slope with, beside her, the sta- the, the dark fire guy with the scimitar, who you only saw in statue form.

DM: [coughs] The... So they're running up a hill, um, and as they run, the, the hill is sort of folding behind them and starting to form into this giant wave of earth. And the land shifts as they go, and it crashes into a what seems like it's maybe a city made out of metal. Um-

DM: ... there's like walls of metal, uh, forming a, a, a perimeter, but there's not much else you can see because the earth crashes into it and tumbles through it and mixes it up, up- upturning and overturning the wall itself. And the two figures running, the ash and the flame, stand for a moment in the center of what once was a city.

DM: The flame creature, uh, blazes—it’s dark fire, but blazes to light for a moment as he holds up the scimitar and makes a few slashing motions. And as he does, the air opens up in a gap. And the world folds, and the remains of the city, like, tumble through the gap, and all that's left here is a valley of ash.

DM: And the scene shifts, and you see now, uh, the two of them running along a, running from something, running down, following the path of a river, which seems much more stable. And behind them is a light that's moving incredibly fast. Like, it's almost like the afterimage of an explosion that's rushing along this river, catching up to them. And as it moves on the river, it's actually sort of shaping and forming the river in a strange inversion of cause and effect. You can see the river ahead of them before it's formed, but the light is forming the river once it gets to them.

DM: And then they get grabbed and tumbled. The, uh, scattered—the flame, dark flame, and the Ash Queen of Frozen Lightning, suddenly [whooshes]— fragmented into 10,000 fragments scattered across what now seems to be Limbo.
DM: And for a long time the mirror is dark. You see, like, the, an occasional flicker of, uh, frozen lightning or sh- you know, cold ash freezing into a sculpture.

DM: [coughs] And then this, the fli- flickers and the pulses get longer. You're clearly in Limbo now as you see from a s- a twisted perspective looking like at a 45-degree angle down at what seems to be a massive line of a thundercloud just drifting across space.

DM: And as it does, everywhere it passes, uh, lightning flashes, and as it flashes things freeze or burst into flames or turn into a wave of sound that blows across as a discordant note until this thundercloud passes across something you can't see because it's beneath the wave of ash.
DM: But as it passes across something it immediately solidifies back into a person, the Queen of Ash, and that's where the mirror vision ends.
Unknown: We should go to Mechanus.
Delwath: We should go to Mechanus.
Seeker: So did she come from there? Is that the implication?
Delwath: No, I think the implication is she came... Before time she was in a war with Mechanus that she lost.

Delwath: And then she was in Limbo, and then the Relic of Order... She... Remember we already knew that she, that the Relic of Order would be possessed by some being of Limbo when they crossed paths randomly. So, like, this Relic that she, that we used—
Delwath: ... recreated her when it crossed paths with her.
DM: So she was just like a random storm front in Limbo with no mind or consciousness until she hit-

Delwath: Right, 'cause she lost the war. The Relic- She, she was destroyed at the end of the war basically. Whatever the war was. It didn't seem like a real one, I mean, like a weird cause and effect war that's taking place without linear time.
Wellby: That suggests she's back to just being a random-
Wellby: ... storm front in Limbo again.
Delwath: Yeah. I think we, we ran away from the storm front in Limbo that she became.
Wellby: I like that, not created or destroyed, we just sort of transformed her.

DM: But the v- the gloss is that the storm fronts have no... It's like they have no will, they have no purpose, they're just like random chaos, so they, there's, they'd never, like, think to invade the material plane or anything.
DM: They just drift across chaos as sort of random events, and it's only when they're solidified into a consciousness that they can have a goal.
Kenzo: And so the Queen of Ash was trying to break into the material plane.
DM: Yeah, that's what Rai and her were fighting about for 30 years.
Unknown: Why was she doing that?
DM: Uh, maybe she w- sh- maybe she didn't realize it was the material plane. She thought she was gonna, like, go back and refight this war or something.
Delwath: Although, wait, she wasn't... It's unclear what she was before.
Delwath: So that implies Limbo was created during the Riving.
Delwath: During the Riving, the, like, the time began.
DM: [coughs] It's metaphysically, metaphysically interesting. Yes. [laughs]
Seeker: So wait, the thing that turned her from a storm into—was the Relic?
Unknown: The thing that we just destroyed?
Unknown: The thing Seeker used to-
DM: The thing Seeker used to move the planes and in the process destroyed it.

before: Kenzo: Oh, it's so cute. There's pl- there's a pie and pumpkins in there.
Unknown: What, what a, what a lovely little...
DM: Delwath made a little feast.
after: Delwath: We should probably, like, go back to Limbo at some point and maybe try and f—I guess there's probably other ones of these drifting around.
Delwath: Sort of like a Sisyphean task probably trying to clear Limbo of whatever's a Relic.

Delwath: Um, that's inter- Like, is that you get one extra action?

after: Unknown: Just that, that one time.

Unknown: We should bring that to Plane of Fire.

interactions.title: The Heartroot creates and repairs its cistern
lines: DM: Uh, you've seen this story of the Heartroot, and so now you, again, before you leave Isingue, you take the, the mirror down to the cistern below the city. And actually, the, it's, the rangers have been doing a lot of work, like clearing things out while you've been sort of guarding the perimeter.
DM: As you go down there, Kenzo, some of the stone now is embedded with these, like, filaments of the Heartroot. Like, it's growing new pillars up-
Unknown: Oh, and by the way-
Kenzo: ... the whole time that the... As soon as... Like, when Kenzo first, like, puts the Heartroot into the cistern, and it's like-
Kenzo: ... Kenzo basically, unless there's like other essential duties or things happening, is just hanging out in the... Like, just hanging out-
Kenzo: ... with the Heartroot and just sort of like observing, helping if nece- and is just, like, all vibes with the Heartroot, and just, you know.
Delwath: You should ask it for a key when we leave.
Kenzo: I already have a key from it.
Unknown: Oh, you already have a key.
Kenzo: No, but I, this, I want this also to be my lair. Like, anytime I come back here I can come and, you know-

DM: Yes. Um, so the first thing you see in the mirror when you hold it up to the cistern is a small sort of green shoot of a root crawling through some dirt, and water rushing along behind it, um, reaching around, sort of grabbing, grasping. And then more roots spring out, um, like the little glowing filamentous, um, kind of... The Heart, right, the Heartroot has like regular roots and then it has those like glowing filamentous, you know, the fungal part.

DM: So it's like a little root reaches through and then more of these things go, and then they start touching the dirt and pushing it away, and more water begins to flood in and flood in. And the dirt begins to, um, grow and compact and shift. And you watch in the mirror over—it's like a sped up version of time—as water begins to flow again, sort of eroding, slowly beginning to erode out a chamber.
DM: And then being channeled, being pushed, like every time one of these little filamentous roots reaches out, water flows along behind it, following it to form a channel.
DM: And over the course of— it's hard to say how much time—decades, centuries, probably not millennia, as you watch in the mirror, like the Heartroot itself slowly begins to excavate this cavern.
DM: And then once there's this big clear area, you see first just a, a lake, like an underground lake like 400 feet across, filled with this perfectly clear, still, greenish-
DM: ... water. Like, not a, not like an algal bloom green, like a clear, pure green. And then slowly you see columns of stone begin to grow up out from the center of the water-

DM: ... forming these twisting spirals. And then roots grow along the ceiling, and more roots grow up from the, from the columns of stone and begin to sprout out through the soil above it. And you watch over the course of another few centuries as the Heartroot grows itself a lair.
Kenzo: Whoa. Is it biomineralizing or something?
DM: It's biomineralizing. It's like your, it's like your bioconcrete.

DM: So the Heartroot, I mean, this was long before Isingue. It grew itself a lair, and then people discovered it and it helped them. But this was its original home, like along the bank of the Istaros River, where it just created a structure it thought was beautiful.
DM: And now it's beginning the slow process of repair.
Kenzo: And the, the whole thing that happened with Limbo that happened here, why did it happen here?
DM: 'Cause Cha'mutte, Isingue was a central piece of the m- of the arm- of the defense against Cha'mutte-
DM: ... and he dropped the plague there.
DM: So the plague was all Limbo magic-
Delwath: He was trying to d- Like we were organizing, I think,
DM: It's all 'cause it was Beryl's home.
DM: Yeah. It was like the heart of the ranger organization.
Delwath: And I don't, I mean, I don't know, remember in high school, but you could imagine Cha'mutte dropping it as an attack and then-
DM: Well, it was, in high school it was supposed to cut off what was then Rohan and Sembara-
DM: ... because the Dunmari armies were-
DM: ... coming to try and relieve the Sembaran armies. And dropping the plague in between them would cut them off.

DM: So Cha'mutte dropped the plague in Isingue. Then when Cha'mutte died, the places that... That was where most of Cha'mutte's magic was actually concentrated. Not where Cha'mutte was, but maintaining the plague.
DM: And so that's where the wound ripped.
Kenzo: Got it, and that was also what started corrupting the Heartroot?
Delwath: I mean, presumably the Heartroot was being corrupted even before Cha'mutte died- Yeah ...
Kenzo: ... from the plague. Yeah, yeah. But— Just because of the plague, yeah.

DM: ... but that's, so that was— that was six month, I mean— right... Plague or whatever... but then the rangers realized what was happening. W—when the plague struck, some of them managed to escape with a fragment of the Heartroot.
Kenzo: And take some of the Heartroot with them. Got it.
DM: And then the rest of the Heartroot eventually got corrupted into the ooze when,
DM: ... when Rai knocked more of Limbo back into the material plane.
Kenzo: Crazy. [sighs] It's a pretty crazy plot.

after: Kenzo: Anything else we want to look at in the mirror? Do you want to look at the, uh, deck of cards or the, the game in the-
DM: So the, the, the bag, you can't...
